notes: Ask each person to write an answer on a sticky note and share it. Agree on the outcomes. Return to these at the close. Allow 10 minutes.
The coach’s own outcome is “Strategy mapped out. New 3HAG.” Hold it back until everyone has shared theirs, so it does not lead the room. It shows on the “Did we get what we came for?” slide.

override.support: Enter today’s split across the four. It totals 100%. Compare it with your last entry.
notes: The team reviews this every second quarter. Each leader enters today’s split, then compares it with the last one.
As leaders hand off functions and hire A-Players, the CEO’s time in execution should fall first.
Allow about 10 minutes.

override.title: Who owns each function now?
override.headline: Who owns each function now?
body: Start a fresh Function Chart. In private mode, each person writes who owns each function.
Reveal, then agree one owner for each. The owner says yes aloud.
Add any function the business now needs.
notes: At the annual, build the Function Chart again on a fresh page. A year of growth changes who does what.
One person is accountable for each function. Others may be responsible for part of the work.
Finish when every function has one owner who said yes out loud.
Allow about 25 minutes, with the Team View after it.

override.support: In Metronome: open KFFM. Put it on the screen.
notes: If the KFFM is not in Metronome yet, show the team’s own KFFM from the board and agree a date to enter it.
Each owner colors their own function by where its critical number stands against target: on track is green, at risk is yellow, needs attention is red. Red is a conversation, not a verdict.
body: The 3 to 5 key functions are still the right ones.
Each owner rates their function red, yellow or green, by its critical number.
What will it take to turn it green?

override.title: For each lever: did you push it? What moved?
override.headline: For each lever: did you push it? What moved?
notes: At a quarterly, the six levers are the check on the KFFM. The KFFM is only right if the team is using it to move more cash faster.

Open the team's own KFFM in Metronome beside this drawing. Go lever by lever. For each one, ask its owner what they did to push it last quarter and what moved. A lever nobody is pushing is a finding. Write it down.
Quantity and conversion: every hand-off has a named widget. Each widget is countable, and it is not revenue or cash. Its owner controls it and counts it every week.
Price: has a good Profit per X emerged? If not, leave it blank.
Timing: add the days each function really took last quarter. Where did the work wait? Which function added the most days? Compare with the days the team estimated last time.
Capacity is how many widgets a function can handle in a month. A function can be fast and still too small.
Cost: what each function costs to run.
Each critical number should tell the owner whether the function is working. Focus on a few, at most four, on the KFFM.
override.support: In Metronome: open KFFM. Go lever by lever.

override.title: Test each Core Value.
override.headline: Test each Core Value.
override.support: Is it a value you hire and fire on, or a brand value?
notes: A value that fails the tests is a brand value or a wish, not a Core Value.
A fourth or fifth value can earn its place here.
Allow about 10 minutes.
body: When did you last let someone go for not living it?
Does someone who keeps breaking it belong here?
Would you build a new company around it, in any industry?
Then ask: is an important value missing?

override.title: Does your BHAG pass?
override.headline: Does your BHAG pass?
override.support: Read your BHAG aloud. Test it.
notes: The BHAG horizon is 10 to 30 years. The third test uses 25 years as one point inside it.
Test leader enthusiasm separately from the whole company’s.
Do not accept an ambition that only repeats today’s business at a larger scale without meaningful stretch.
At the annual, the team has just agreed the BHAG. If a test fails, go back to the circle it fails on.

override.title: Is your Market Map still right?
override.headline: Is your Market Map still right?
notes: Put the team’s own Market Map on the screen. The example here is a reminder of its parts.
Ask what changed in the market this year: a new competitor, a channel that grew, a supplier that gained power.
Update the map now, or put the update on the homework list.
override.support: In Metronome: open War Room. Put your Market Map on the screen. What changed this year?

override.title: Start from your 3HAG line.
override.headline: Start from your 3HAG line.
override.support: Put your own agreed line on the screen. This one is the example.
notes: At the annual, this is a reminder. The line is agreed. The example shows the line that the next slides make true.
Competitors can copy what you add. They cannot copy what you drop without breaking their own business.
In the example, reporting and customization drop, so that setup, price and support can lead.
Close Day 1. Recap the Core Purpose, the BHAG, the new 3HAG, its differentiators and the swim lanes. Note open questions for tomorrow.

override.title: How did the year go?
override.headline: How did the year go?
override.support: In Metronome: open One Page Plans. Review the 1HAG, then the last QHAG.
notes: At the annual, the 1HAG is closing. Review the whole year first, then the last quarter.
Everyone updated their status in Metronome before today.
Close each priority on two questions: was it done, and did it succeed?
Ask where the estimates were wrong and what the team learned. That is what next year’s numbers are built on.
Allow about 40 minutes.

panels.heading: What does it build or move?
panels.support: A differentiator, or a KFFM lever that brings cash in faster.

panels.heading: How much will it move a critical number?
panels.support: Name the number and the target. If it barely moves, think twice.

panels.heading: How soon will we see it?
panels.support: Name the date the measure of success will be achieved by. If it takes a long time to show, think twice.

panels.heading: Who can own it and succeed?
panels.support: One person, with the capacity and the skills to deliver it.

panels.heading: What will it cost?
panels.support: Money, time and attention. Choose the most impact for the least cost.

notes: Ask these six questions of every candidate. Keep the few that contribute most: ideally 3, up to 5. A routine task list is not a set of company priorities.
Builds: fix the cause, not the symptom. An annual priority builds a differentiator or moves a KFFM lever.

Impact and speed are the two warning signs. If the impact takes a long time to show, or it barely moves a critical number, think twice. There can be good reasons to go ahead anyway, but weigh both every time.

Owner: can one person be accountable? Do they have the time, given what they already carry? Do they have the skills, or the support, to succeed? If no one fits, the priority is not ready, or the first step is to find the owner.
Risk: ask how badly this could go wrong.

Once chosen, ask an owner to claim each priority aloud and agree the done-by date, the measure and the date it will be achieved by. If two priorities compete for the same people or cash, agree which one wins. Done and success are different dates. The work is done by one date. The number has moved by a later one.
Hover over “KFFM lever” to show the six levers.
Read the new 1HAG aloud, top to bottom, then run the six checks. Each priority must move its number enough, and soon enough to see.
Check the priorities against the first four quarters of the swim lanes and against what was burning on the KFFM yesterday.
Change only what fails. Anything that cannot be fixed now goes on the homework list with an owner.
override.support: Read your new 1HAG aloud from the board before you move on.
body: Every number and priority has one owner with capacity.
Each priority builds a differentiator or moves a KFFM lever.
No priority invests in an attribute you chose to let drop.
Each measure has a target and an achieved-by date.
The targets keep you on track for the 3HAG.
The widgets support the revenue, and head count is set.

notes: Every leader independently lists what must be accomplished this quarter to deliver a 1HAG priority, then shares.
At the annual, the candidates include last quarter’s open priorities, the first quarter of each swim lane, and anything burning on the KFFM.
Done is not the same as success. Each priority has a done-by date for the work and an achieved-by date for the result.
Run the six questions on each candidate. Hover over “six questions” to show them.
The team ranks the survivors together. Pick the #1 priority first. Give it one owner.
override.support: What must you get done now to deliver the 1HAG?
body: List candidates: open priorities, 1HAG priorities, the lever you picked and Q1 of your swim lanes.
Test each with the six questions, then rank.
Agree on the owner, done-by date, measure of success and achieved-by date.
Connect each to a 1HAG priority. Give each an owner, a done-by date, a measure of success and an achieved-by date.
override.title: What else must you get done this quarter?
override.headline: What else must you get done this quarter?

override.support: Read your new QHAG aloud from the board before you move on.

notes: Start with the widgets, then take the priorities in rank order. The owner of each lane drafts it and the team questions it.
Building the plan together develops the team as much as the plan.
Allow about 45 minutes.
Homework: add each lane’s steps as sub-priorities under its company priority in Metronome.
Widgets: a weekly number shows a miss while there is time to act. Ask each owner: can you reach this week’s number? The weekly numbers add up to the quarter’s targets.
Lanes: the team sees each week how the priority gets done. Lanes belong to company priorities, never to a function. Each lane keeps its priority’s owner.

Steps: a step can be a decision made, a test run, a result verified or a checkpoint. It only has to be real and checkable. A live priority that cannot name its weekly work is too vague, or too small for a lane.
override.support: Work together on the 13-Week Sprint Lanes page of your board.

notes: If the answer is no, change the plan now. Move a step, change an owner or drop a priority.
Lanes show the work. They are not the measure of success. That stays on the QHAG.
The weekly leadership meeting reviews sprint lane status.

override.headline: How are your meetings going?
override.title: How are your meetings going?
override.support: In Metronome: open Meetings. Running? Working? What to change? Rate each: 0 below, 1 meets, 2 exceeds.

panels.heading: Daily huddle
panels.support: 7 to 10 minutes, every day except the day of the weekly meeting.

panels.heading: Weekly 1:1
panels.support: 15 to 30 minutes. Each leader with each direct report, led by the direct report.

panels.heading: Weekly leadership meeting
panels.support: 60 minutes or less. The CEO owns it.

panels.heading: Monthly Town Hall
panels.support: 30 to 45 minutes. Everyone. The CEO owns it.

notes: Give it about 10 minutes.
Rate each meeting: 0 below, 1 meets, 2 exceeds expectations.
Quarterly Planning is the fifth meeting. The team is in it now.
Daily huddle: Good news; Metrics: yesterday’s widget actual and today’s forecast; The #1 thing to get done today; Stucks, and anything that can’t wait.
Weekly 1:1: Good news; Metrics; Top 3 priorities for the week; Feedback both ways; Dynamic.
Weekly leadership meeting: Good news; Values recognition; Widget scoreboard; KFFM critical numbers; QHAG: numbers, priorities, sprint lanes; Stucks, asks and offers.

Monthly Town Hall: Good news, then values recognition; QHAG progress on the #1 priority, and how everyone can help; Financial transparency: what is working and what is not; One thing we can do as a company to improve our financial health.
Values recognition: name someone in front of the whole company. Name the value. Name what they did.
This is the only meeting where the whole company hears the same thing at the same time.
Financial transparency builds the financial literacy of the whole company.
Show the Team View at a Town Hall only when it changes.
The daily huddle’s facilitator rotates.
The scoreboard shows last week’s widget forecast, the actual and this week’s forecast.

override.support: Write them together now. Each leader shares them with their team tomorrow.
override.title: What 3 messages will you share with the whole company?
override.headline: What 3 messages will you share with the whole company?
notes: Write the messages together and read them aloud. Keep them specific to the agreed plan. Prepare leaders to deliver a consistent message to the whole company.
Every leader shares the messages with their team the day after.
Close the session. Recap how the plan connects, from the 3HAG differentiators to this quarter’s priorities, and when the next daily huddle is. Then invite everyone to answer.
